senses.definition: someone that you do not know or have never met before

examples.en: Children should never talk to strangers on the street.
examples.vi: Trẻ em không bao giờ nên nói chuyện với người lạ trên đường.

senses.vi: người lạ mặt; người xa lạ

senses.definition: someone who is new to a particular place, city, or community

examples.en: I am a stranger here, so can you give me directions?
examples.vi: Tôi là người mới đến đây, bạn có thể chỉ đường giúp tôi không?

senses.definition: a playful way to refer to a friend you have not seen for a long time

examples.en: Hello stranger! Where have you been hiding all these months?
examples.vi: Chào người lạ ơi! Mấy tháng nay bạn trốn ở đâu thế?

senses.vi: người quen lâu ngày không gặp

thesaurus.definition: anyone who does not belong in the environment in which they are found
an individual that one is not acquainted with

vi_block: Người lạ mặt, người xa lạ.

examples: That gentleman is a stranger to me.
Children are taught not to talk to strangers.
wiktionary.gloss: A person whom one does not know; a person who is neither a friend nor an acquaintance.
An outsider or foreigner.
One not admitted to communion or fellowship.
A newcomer.

examples: Hello, stranger!
wiktionary.gloss: Used ironically to refer to a person who the speaker knows.

examples: Actual possession of land gives a good title against a stranger having no title.
wiktionary.gloss: One not privy or party to an act, contract, or title; a mere intruder or intermeddler; one who interferes without right.
A moth, Lacanobia blenna

idioms.gloss: Sometimes actual events are stranger than imagined ones.
To be familiar with due to past experience.
Used to express that even though an event or idea seems very unusual or surprising, it is still possible.

tatoeba.vi: Chúng tôi không phải là người lạ.
Một người lạ đã bắt chuyện với tôi.
Tôi không bao giờ tin người lạ.

tatoeba.en: A stranger spoke to me on the bus.
tatoeba.vi: Một người lạ đã nói chuyện với tôi trên xe buýt.

thesaurus.definition: a sign visible from the street

wiktionary.gloss: a sign showing the name of a street, usually placed at a street corner.

blocks.etymology: Learned borrowing from Medieval Latin subsūmere, from sub- + sūmō (“to take”). Compare English consume.

senses.definition: to include or put something into a larger or more general group or rule

examples.en: All these smaller departments were subsumed into a single ministry.
examples.vi: Tất cả các phòng ban nhỏ này đã được sáp nhập vào một bộ duy nhất.

thesaurus.definition: contain or include
consider (an instance of something) as part of a general rule or principle

examples: Near-synonym: comprise
wiktionary.gloss: To place (any one cognition) under another as belonging to it; to include or contain something else.
To consider an occurrence as part of a principle or rule.

blocks.etymology: Popularized by the "Erm, What the Sigma?" meme which originated around March 2024, although usage dates back to 2020.

examples: What the skibidi is she doing to that cat?
How the skibidi am I supposed to come up with this month's rent?
wiktionary.gloss: Used for emphasis after an interrogative word or relative pronoun.

examples: You have to accept that a new world pushes out the old. The wheel turns.
wiktionary.gloss: Time moves forward; circumstances change; life continues.

blocks.etymology: Borrowed from French toucan, borrowed from Old Tupi tukana, from Proto-Tupi-Guarani *tũkãn, from Proto-Tupian *jɨokãn.

thesaurus.definition: brilliantly colored arboreal fruit-eating bird of tropical America having a very large thin-walled beak

vi_block: Cả hai (người đi bộ và người lái xe đạp) đều qua được.

wiktionary.gloss: Any of various neotropical frugivorous birds from the family Ramphastidae, with a large colorful beak.

blocks.etymology: Back-formation from troubleshooter; by surface analysis, trouble + shoot.

thesaurus.definition: solve problems

examples: Near-synonyms: debug, diagnose, check, investigate
wiktionary.gloss: To analyze or diagnose (a problem, or something faulty) to the point of determining a solution.

blocks.etymology: From un- + acquirable.
vi_block: Không thể mua được, không thể tạu được.

wiktionary.gloss: That cannot be acquired.

blocks.etymology: From un- + intoxicating.
vi_block: Không kích thích, không kích động.

wiktionary.gloss: Not intoxicating.

senses.definition: showing feelings or behaviour openly and without control

examples.en: The children shouted with unrestrained excitement.
examples.vi: Bọn trẻ la hét trong niềm phấn khích không thể kìm nén.

senses.vi: không bị kiềm chế; không bị nén lại

senses.definition: not held back or kept in place physically

examples.en: Passengers should not travel unrestrained in the back of the car.
examples.vi: Hành khách không nên ngồi ở hàng ghế sau xe mà không thắt dây an toàn.

senses.vi: không bị giữ lại; được thả lỏng

thesaurus.definition: marked by uncontrolled excitement or emotion

vi_block: Không bị kiềm chế, không bị nén lại, không bị dằn lại, được thả lỏng.

examples: The party was a scene of unrestrained debauchery.
wiktionary.gloss: Immoderate; not restrained or held in check; inordinate (literary).

examples: Their meeting was one of unrestrained joy.
wiktionary.gloss: Spontaneous, natural and informal; unconstrained.
Not subject to physical restraint.

blocks.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *n̥- From un- + substantiated.

senses.definition: not supported or proved by facts or reliable evidence

examples.en: The newspaper retracted the unsubstantiated claims against the minister.
examples.vi: Tờ báo đã rút lại những tuyên bố không có căn cứ nhắm vào vị bộ trưởng.

senses.vi: không có căn cứ; không được chứng minh

thesaurus.definition: unsupported by other evidence

vi_block: Không được chứng minh, không có căn cứ.

wiktionary.gloss: Lacking substantiation; without evidence.
Synonym of vibrancy.

thesaurus.definition: a warning to take action concerning something that was overlooked or neglected
a telephone call that you request be made at a specific time in order to wake you up

examples: She requested a five a.m. wake-up call from the front desk.
wiktionary.gloss: A telephone call to awaken someone at a certain time, especially one requested by the person while staying at a hotel.

examples: Near-synonym: reality check
The recent deaths should serve as a wake-up call to others at risk.
wiktionary.gloss: An alert, reminder, or call to action caused by a dramatic event.
